verdict.rationale: Brex lets admins define spend policies, limits and multi-level approval rules. The product then applies them automatically on transaction events: it blocks out-of-policy purchases, routes approvals by amount, vendor or role, and auto-approves low-risk expenses. These rules are limited to spend, policy and approval domains rather than a general event-to-action rule builder, and the evidence is marketing copy only. Webhooks and Zapier, Workato or Pipedream are developer building blocks or third-party tools, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a general-purpose user-defined event-to-action rule engine, technical docs for configuring rules (UI or API), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Set rules for how employees can spend, what they need to document, and who needs to approve. Brex AI applies them to every transaction.
Automatically block out-of-policy purchases, with preset rules and limits.
Tailor multi-level approval flows based on amount, vendor, employee role, and more — and Brex will route for you automatically
Your review agent auto-approves low-risk expenses and requests, escalates exceptions, and follows up with anyone out of compliance.
